solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Piece supporting German philosopher reportedly shot

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other, so it comes second
reportedly signals that the philosopher's name is to be taken as it is heard, not as spelt

parts.note: Karl Marx was the German philosopher behind Das Kapital
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A gunman shoots a German thinker while some piece of equipment props him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes MARX sound like MARKS; 'supporting' puts MAN beneath it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A good shot is a person skilled with a gun, a crack marksman.

clue.text: Composer almost makes party

indicators.note: almost means the composer's name stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Boléro

explanation.surface: A composer nearly throws a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter, L, from RAVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large lively party, especially a dance event with loud music.

clue.text: Data included in offer for engine part

indicators.note: included in means the data word is placed inside the offer word

parts.note: a bid is an offer, as at an auction
gen is British slang for information or data

explanation.surface: Information comes bundled with a sales offer for a car component.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The big end is the larger end of an engine's connecting rod, fitted round the crankshaft.

clue.text: Salvo — first to be fired, by the way

indicators.note: the first letter is dismissed, fired like an employee, so it is removed

parts.note: a broadside is a salvo from all the guns on one side of a ship

explanation.surface: Gunners discuss which shot in a salvo will be fired first, incidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests gunnery but means sacked: 'first to be fired' drops B from BROADSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something by the way lies at the roadside, the edge of the road.

clue.text: Museum, close to street overlooking Notre Dame, in need of attention

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece overlooking another sits above it, so comes first
close to here means the final letter of the following word
something in need of attention is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Paris cathedral beside a street is looking dilapidated and wants repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' gives T from street; 'in need of attention' rearranges NOTREDAME into ATEMODERN, which 'overlooking' places below the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tate Modern is London's national gallery of modern art, a museum on the South Bank.

clue.text: Fish one caught in lodge

indicators.note: caught in means the numeral is trapped inside the other word

parts.note: to lodge something is to place it, put it in position
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single fish is landed at a fishing lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish common in European waters and on British menus.

clue.text: Model soldier, like leader of military

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
to dig something is slang for liking it

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A model soldier resembles the commander of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' is a verb here, slang DIG, not a comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a model or typical example to follow.

clue.text: Son embraced by mother and mentor

indicators.note: embraced by means the son's letter is held within the mother word

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, used in old-fashioned British slang

explanation.surface: A boy is hugged by his mother and his teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A master can be a teacher or guide, as a mentor is.

clue.text: By word of mouth round mass meeting

parts.note: O is round in shape
a rally is a mass gathering of supporters

explanation.surface: News of a big gathering spreads round by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Orally means spoken rather than written, passed by speech.

clue.text: Extremities of Sark, the ancient island

indicators.note: extremities are the outermost parts, so the first and last letters

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: Someone describes the edges of Sark, an old island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is a small Channel Island, a fine decoy for another island.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is a large island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: I see today's cryptic may make one be careful

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and disguised, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A solver warns that this puzzle could make anyone cautious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' rearranges ISEETODAYS; 'may make one' links fodder to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy does it is an idiom urging someone to go gently and carefully.

clue.text: A goddess duke entertained

parts.note: the Muses were the Greek goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: A goddess entertained a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused means entertained, kept pleasantly occupied.

clue.text: Jack's chance to sample a port?

definitions.text: Jack's chance to sample a port?

parts.words: Jack's chance to sample a port?
parts.note: Jack is a sailor (Jack Tar); his opportunity to visit a harbour town is time off the ship, not a drink of port wine

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack gets the chance to taste some port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink and 'Jack' a name, but Jack Tar is a sailor and the port is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore leave is time a sailor is allowed off ship, to go ashore at a port.

clue.text: Speedo is rigged in phases

indicators.note: something rigged is fixed or arranged differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer's Speedo is kitted out in stages.
explanation.walkthrough: Speedo is a brand of swimwear; 'rigged' rearranges SPEEDOIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are distinct parts or stages in a sequence, as phases are.

clue.text: Silly person, old one in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble means disturbed or upset, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool, an old person in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal for a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Distribution of gifts in big steamship, English

parts.note: large means big

explanation.surface: An Englishman hands out presents aboard a large steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving, money or gifts handed out freely.

clue.text: Very bad being always bound in two directions

indicators.note: bound in means held inside the other letters as if tied

parts.note: S and E are compass points south and east
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Someone is always tied up going two ways at once, a terrible state.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or serious, as a very bad illness is.

clue.text: Mysterious coteries formed

indicators.note: formed means shaped anew, so the letters are made into a new word

explanation.surface: Secretive little cliques have been set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a few insiders, obscure.

clue.text: Falcon kept in brighter cellar

indicators.note: kept in means the letters are held within these neighbouring words

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is kept in a lighter cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tercel is a male falcon or hawk, used in falconry.

clue.text: Not bothered about heartless judge

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: a referee judges a match

explanation.surface: Someone is unconcerned about a judge without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the central E of REFEREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free of worry, untroubled.

clue.text: Entice everyone onto river at Ripon

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece goes onto the second, so it sits above it

parts.note: all means everyone
the Ure is a Yorkshire river flowing through Ripon

explanation.surface: Someone tempts the whole crowd down to the riverside at Ripon.
explanation.walkthrough: Ripon is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to attract or tempt, to entice.

clue.text: Worthless metal trophy

parts.note: tin is a metal
pot is slang for a sporting trophy or cup

explanation.surface: A cheap metal cup awarded as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot means inferior or of little worth, as a tinpot dictator.

clue.text: Gift adult left in shelter

indicators.note: in means the two letters are put inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up left a present in the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or aptitude.

clue.text: Censor pornographic writer

parts.note: blue means indecent or pornographic, as in a blue film
a pencil is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A censor deals with an author of smut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is not an author but the instrument that writes.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil is to cut or censor text, from the editor's blue pencil.

clue.text: A base in a port near the Red Sea

definitions.text: a port near the Red Sea

parts.note: a den is a base or hideout

explanation.surface: A naval base is located in a port by the Red Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a port city in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: A bishop, the Spanish murder victim

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish bishop is the victim of a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, the first murder victim.

clue.text: Accent on southern French wine

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed next to, so the accent comes before the S

parts.note: a grave is an accent mark, as in è

explanation.surface: A southern French wine is pronounced with an accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a wine region of Bordeaux, and its wine.

clue.text: Cause of one leering, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something that might make a person ogle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges I and LEERING; the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie, women's underwear, might make an onlooker leer.
